sections.h2: Selling a house in Radnor Township
sections.html:
Radnor is a Main Line township in Delaware County with high home values, a use and occupancy certificate required for every resale, and a transfer tax above the county default. Home values run above $800,000, so many buyers arrive with jumbo loans, tough appraisals and long inspection lists. About a third of households rent, which keeps investors and landlords in the buyer pool near Villanova University and Eastern University.

Wayne, St. Davids, Rosemont, Ithan, Garrett Hill and Villanova all fall in or touch the township. Strafford, Bryn Mawr and Villanova straddle township lines, so the mailing address on a listing may not match the municipality. That matters for both the transfer tax and the certificate, so check the municipality on your deed before anything is filed.

sections.h2: Use and occupancy certificate for a resale
sections.html:
Every resale needs a use and occupancy permit, and the township Engineering Department issues it. No new owner may move in until the certificate is out, so treat it as a closing item, not an afterthought.

  • The seller files the application at least 10 business days before settlement. The owner signs it, and the fee is $150.
  • Filing 10 days or less before settlement adds a $300 expedite fee.
  • The township inspects for house number display and the condition of the public sidewalk, then sends a violation notice for anything that needs repair.
  • If sidewalk blocks cannot be replaced before closing, money goes into escrow with the department, and a sidewalk permit is needed for the work.
  • Seller and buyer both sign a smoke detector and carbon monoxide certification. The township will not accept the application unless the form, the fee and the signed application arrive together.
  • The owner books an inside look at the sanitary sewer soil pipe to confirm there are no illegal connections. Sump pumps must be disconnected from the sanitary system under Chapter 235 of the township code.

Call the Engineering Department at 610-688-5600, extension 129, to book the sewer appointment. Do it the day you file, because that appointment is the step most likely to push a closing date.

Delaware County's Recorder of Deeds shows the state share at 1% and the local share at 1% for most municipalities. Radnor Township is named as an exception at 1.5% local. Confirm the exact split with the Recorder before you set a net-proceeds number.

The county Recorder collects the state's 1% along with any local tax. The seller (grantor) and the buyer (grantee) are jointly liable, which is why the sales agreement should say who pays. Certain transfers between family members, and property passed by will or intestate succession, are exempt under state rules, so an inherited house moving to an heir is treated differently from a market sale.

The recording office is at the Government Center in Media. If a deed leaves the price off, the state's Statement of Value form (REV-183) carries the value to the Recorder.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and appeals
sections.html:
Township bills go out on or before February 1, and the face amount is due May 31. Paying by March 31 earns a 2% discount, and a 10% penalty applies after May 31. The Radnor School District bills and collects its own tax separately, with school bills mailed in July.

An unpaid bill becomes a lien if it is not paid by the end of the calendar year, and the Delaware County Tax Claim Bureau adds interest and penalties. When a house sells, return the bill to the township with the new owner's name, because the Recorder can take more than 60 days to process a title transfer.

  • Assessment appeals go to the Delaware County Board of Assessment Appeals before August 1, for a value effective the following January 1.
  • An appeal does not pause the bill. You pay what is billed and receive a refund or credit if the value drops.
  • The county reassessment that ran from December 2017 to 2020 took effect in January 2021, so current values rest on that base year.
  • A tax certification from the township finance office costs $25 per parcel, and title companies typically request one.

Sewer and stormwater are billed together on a separate mailing around April 1, due May 31. The stormwater charge depends on parcel size and applies to all developed properties in the township.

Three paths cover most sellers, and each handles the township certificate differently.

  • A traditional listing suits houses in good repair. The agent coordinates the certificate, but showings, inspection requests and buyer financing set the schedule.
  • A for-sale-by-owner sale saves the commission and leaves you running the certificate, the sewer inspection and the transfer tax paperwork yourself.
  • A cash sale to a company that buys as-is removes lender timing and repairs from the buyer side. The seller still files the township application and still schedules the sewer check, so ask any buyer who does the filing and who pays any sidewalk escrow.

Compare offers on net proceeds, not headline price. Subtract the transfer tax, the $150 or $300 township fee, any sidewalk or sewer repairs and unpaid taxes before you decide.

sections.h2: A timeline for a fast Radnor closing
sections.html:
Start the day you sign a sales agreement. Gather your deed, the latest township and school tax bills, and the parcel (folio) number, because the application and the tax certification both ask for them.

  1. File the occupancy application with the Engineering Department and pay the $150 fee, so you stay clear of the $300 expedite charge.
  2. Call 610-688-5600, extension 129, and book the sewer soil pipe inspection for the earliest open slot.
  3. Walk the front of the property. Check the house number and look for lifted or cracked sidewalk blocks, since those are the items the township flags.
  4. Have the buyer and yourself sign the smoke detector and carbon monoxide certification and send it in with the application.
  5. Ask the township finance office for the tax certification the title company will want.
  6. Confirm with the closing agent that the deed, the Statement of Value if needed, and the transfer tax will reach the Recorder together.

A cash buyer can skip the mortgage appraisal and underwriting wait, which are the slowest parts of a financed sale in a high-value market. The township steps above stay the same either way, so the earliest you can close is set by how fast you complete them.

sections.h2: Selling with taxes owed or repairs outstanding
sections.html:
Unpaid township or school tax does not block a sale. It gets paid from your proceeds at closing, and the title company asks for a tax certification to see what is owed. If a bill has already turned into a lien, the Delaware County Tax Claim Bureau adds interest and penalties, so the number grows the longer you wait.

Repairs work the same way. The sewer, sidewalk and house number items the township flags must be corrected or escrowed before the certificate is released. Cosmetic and structural repairs are a matter between you and the buyer, and a cash buyer who takes the house as-is simply prices them in.

faqs.q: Who applies for the certificate of occupancy in Radnor?
faqs.a: The seller does. The application goes to the Radnor Engineering Department at least 10 business days before settlement, signed by the owner, with the $150 fee and the smoke detector and carbon monoxide form signed by seller and buyer.

faqs.q: What happens if my sidewalk is damaged at the time of sale?
faqs.a: The township sends a violation notice after its inspection. If the sidewalk blocks cannot be replaced before settlement, money is placed in escrow with the Engineering Department, and a sidewalk permit is required for the repair.

faqs.q: Is Radnor's transfer tax higher than the rest of Delaware County?
faqs.a: Yes. Most municipalities sit at the 1% default local share, while Radnor Township is at 1.5%, plus the 1% state tax. Ask the Recorder of Deeds to confirm the combined figure for your deed.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Radnor house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, but the sewer connection, sidewalk and house number items flagged by the township still have to be corrected or escrowed before the certificate is released. Cosmetic and structural repairs are between you and the buyer.

faqs.q: Where do I get a Radnor tax certification for closing?
faqs.a: From the Radnor Township finance office at 301 Iven Avenue in Wayne. The township charges $25 per certification, and you need the parcel (folio) number, the owner name and the address.
